intent: Bring python_pkg/app_icons/_glyph_art.py (253 lines) back under the 250-line cap without discarding the lyricanki note-ascender glyph that pushed it over. This is the last blocker to wiring the cap into pre-commit.
scope: python_pkg/app_icons/glyphs.py: imports _NOTE_ASCENDER and _TRACK_BARS from the new module
Non-goal: any change to the glyph artwork itself
changes: Moved the two most recent glyph constants (_TRACK_BARS, _NOTE_ASCENDER) with their comments into a companion module. The division carries no meaning beyond the cap, and the module docstring says so, because a reader would otherwise look for a taxonomy that is not there.

glyphs.py imports from both modules. Nothing else changed: the Glyph dataclass, the registry and the lookup all stay put, so no caller or test needs to know which file a glyph lives in — the same contract the original _glyph_art split established.

verification.evidence: 13 glyphs load; both moved names ('note-ascender', 'track-bars') are present in the registry.

verification.command: build_svg(GLYPHS[name], '#7C9CF5', with_background=True) for the moved glyphs
verification.evidence: Ran the real renderer, not just the import: note-ascender produces 641 bytes and track-bars 444, both with the accent colour substituted. A control glyph (anvil, untouched) renders alongside them at 496 bytes.
44 passed. The coverage gate reports below 100% only because a single-package run does not exercise the rest of the repo.
'all checked files are within 250 lines'. Both modules are under: 208 and 50.
ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, pytest-with-coverage and codespell all pass. No suppression added.

risks: A mid-edit slip removed the _NOTE_ASCENDER argument from its Glyph(...) call site as well as from the import list, which surfaced immediately as a TypeError on import. Repaired and re-verified by rendering; recorded because the import-only check would not have caught it — the registry has to be built for that failure to appear.
Two modules now hold glyph data, so someone adding a glyph must pick one. The docstring directs them to the cap rather than to a false distinction.
rollback: git revert the commit; _glyph_art.py returns to 253 lines and the file-length gate cannot be wired until it is under 250 again.
